must_remember: Stimulated emission produces a photon strictly in phase, of the same frequency, polarization, and direction as the incident photon.
Population inversion ($N_2 > N_1$) is a non-equilibrium state essential for laser action and requires external pumping.
A metastable state possesses a relatively long lifetime (typically $10^{-3} \text{ s}$) compared to ordinary excited states ($10^{-8} \text{ s}$).
Four-level laser systems are more efficient than three-level systems because the lower laser level rapidly empties into the ground state, lowering the threshold.
The Einstein A and B ratio is given by $\frac{A_{21}}{B_{21}} = \frac{8\pi h \nu^3}{c^3}$, connecting spontaneous and stimulated emission probabilities.

glossary.meaning: A non-thermal equilibrium condition where the population of atoms in a higher energy level exceeds that of a lower energy level ($N_2 > N_1$).
An intermediate excited energy state with an unusually long lifetime, crucial for accumulating atoms to achieve population inversion.
The process of using high-intensity light sources such as flashlamps or secondary lasers to excite atoms to higher energy levels.
An arrangement of mirrors that reflects light back and forth through the active laser medium, providing feedback and amplification.
Coefficients ($A_{21}, B_{12}, B_{21}$) quantifying the probabilities of spontaneous emission, stimulated absorption, and stimulated emission.
